test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 26 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The selling price of a book is Rs. 855. If the loss incurred through the sale is 10%, then what is the nominal amount of loss incurred?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss of 10% means **Selling Price (SP)** is 90% of the **Cost Price (CP)**.

Given SP = Rs. 855, which represents 90% of the value.

Nominal **Loss** (10%) = (855 ÷ 90) × 10

Nominal Loss = 855 ÷ 9 = 95

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = Rs. 855

**Loss Percentage** = 10%

**Formula Used:**

1. Cost Price (CP) = [Selling Price × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%]

2. Nominal Loss = Cost Price − Selling Price

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/225e988983fe09b6a24d166689ae693fc1742deb8f036e612c35407de888010a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [855 × 100] ÷ [100 − 10]

⇒ CP = 85500 ÷ 90

⇒ CP = 950

⇒ Nominal Loss = CP − SP

⇒ Nominal Loss = 950 − 855

⇒ Nominal Loss = 95

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when SP > CP, and Loss occurs when CP > SP. Profit or Loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless otherwise stated.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always offered on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount. Discount% = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

Two successive discounts of a% and b% are equivalent to a single discount of [a + b − (ab ÷ 100)]%.</p
